  ## Task: Expected customer-redress risk score

  A customer-redress team assesses the operational and conduct risk of each case. Assume all sampled quantities are independent.

  - The agent’s conduct is `"professional"`, `"snigger"`, or `"dismissive"` with probabilities 0.82, 0.06, and 0.12, respectively. The conduct condition is met if the agent is recorded to snigger.
  - Base handling time, in minutes, follows a gamma distribution with shape 4 and scale 2.5.
  - The redress offer, in dollars, follows a gamma distribution with shape 5 and scale 20.
  - Additional handling time is one minute per $25 of redress offered, so total handling time is base handling time plus the redress offer divided by 25.
  - The number of minutes the team can spare follows a uniform distribution from 8 to 18 minutes. Remaining spare time equals this allowance minus total handling time.
  - The service achievement is to offer at least $80 in redress.

  Assign risk points as follows:

  - 5 points if the agent’s conduct is `"snigger"`;
  - 3 points if total handling time exceeds 15 minutes;
  - 4 points if the redress offer is below the $80 achievement target;
  - 2 points if remaining spare time is below zero.

  The case risk score is the sum of all applicable points. Using simulation, estimate the expected case risk score.

  ## Reference solution

  ```text
  conduct ~ discrete(values=["professional", "snigger", "dismissive"], probabilities=[0.82, 0.06, 0.12])
  base_minutes ~ gamma(a=4, scale=2.5)
  redress_offer ~ gamma(a=5, scale=20)
  minutes_team_can_spare ~ uniform(loc=8, scale=10)
  total_minutes = base_minutes + (redress_offer / 25)
  remaining_spare_minutes = minutes_team_can_spare - total_minutes
  snigger_condition = conduct == "snigger"
  minute_condition = total_minutes > 15
  achievement_condition = redress_offer < 80
  spare_condition = remaining_spare_minutes < 0
  risk_score = (5 * snigger_condition) + ((3 * minute_condition) + ((4 * achievement_condition) + (2 * spare_condition)))
  return risk_score
  ```

  ## Task: Recreation Centre Chicken Kitchen Upgrade Cost

  A recreation centre is upgrading its chicken-preparation kitchen. A stricter food-safety operating discipline will outmode some existing preparation stations, while the exterior walls must be insulated.

  Assume all uncertain quantities are mutually independent:

  - The wall area to insulate is uniformly distributed between 115 and 135 m².
  - The insulation cost per square metre follows a lognormal distribution with shape parameter 0.18 and scale parameter £82/m².
  - The number of outmoded chicken-preparation stations follows a Poisson distribution with mean 3.2.
  - A contractor’s realized replacement cost per outmoded station, applied to every station replaced, follows a gamma distribution with shape 9 and scale £1,400.
  - Recreation activities will be closed for 2, 3, 5, or 7 days with probabilities 0.2, 0.4, 0.3, and 0.1, respectively.
  - The lost recreation margin per closure day follows a normal distribution with mean £1,800 and standard deviation £250.
  - A closure lasting at least 5 days is an extended closure and incurs an additional fixed inspection cost of £4,500.

  Total project cost is the sum of insulation cost, station-replacement cost, lost recreation margin, and any extended-closure inspection cost.

  Estimate the expected total project cost and its 90th percentile, in pounds.

  ## Reference solution

  ```text
  wall_area ~ uniform(loc=115, scale=20)
  insulation_rate ~ lognorm(s=0.18, scale=82)
  outmoded_stations ~ poisson(mu=3.2)
  station_cost ~ gamma(a=9, scale=1400)
  closure_days ~ discrete(values=[2, 3, 5, 7], probabilities=[0.2, 0.4, 0.3, 0.1])
  lost_recreation_margin ~ norm(loc=1800, scale=250)
  extended_closure = closure_days >= 5
  insulation_cost = wall_area * insulation_rate
  replacement_cost = outmoded_stations * station_cost
  closure_cost = closure_days * lost_recreation_margin
  inspection_cost = extended_closure * 4500
  total_cost = (insulation_cost + replacement_cost) + (closure_cost + inspection_cost)
  ```

  ## Task: Precious-metal conversion shortfall

  A refinery processes deposits from a group of precious-metal depositors during one operating period.

  - The number of depositors is Poisson distributed with mean 24.
  - The average gross mass received per depositor is Gamma distributed with shape 9 and scale 4 kg. Total gross mass is the number of depositors multiplied by this average mass.
  - The common fine-metal purity fraction is Beta distributed with parameters \(38\) and \(2\).
  - The fraction of fine metal diverted into an unrecoverable side stream is Beta distributed with parameters \(2\) and \(98\).
  - The refinery selects one conversion process for the period. Its conversion yield is categorical: 0.94 with probability 0.15, 0.97 with probability 0.60, and 0.99 with probability 0.25.
  - Gross fine-metal mass equals total gross mass multiplied by purity.
  - Converted mass equals gross fine-metal mass multiplied by the conversion yield and by one minus the side-stream fraction.
  - Conditional on the number of depositors, the number of accounts that must be reinstated is Binomial distributed with that number of trials and probability 0.08 per depositor.
  - The average fine-metal mass required to reinstate each affected account is Gamma distributed with shape 2.5 and scale 1.2 kg. Total reinstated mass is the reinstatement count multiplied by this average mass.
  - Net deliverable mass is converted mass minus total reinstated mass.

  All sampled quantities are mutually independent except for the stated dependence of the reinstatement count on the number of depositors. Gamma distributions use shape and scale parameters.

  Estimate the probability that net deliverable fine-metal mass is less than 780 kg.

  ## Reference solution

  ```text
  depositor_count ~ poisson(mu=24)
  mass_per_depositor ~ gamma(a=9, scale=4)
  purity ~ beta(a=38, b=2)
  side_fraction ~ beta(a=2, b=98)
  conversion_yield ~ discrete(values=[0.94, 0.97, 0.99], probabilities=[0.15, 0.6, 0.25])
  reinstatement_count ~ binom(n=depositor_count, p=0.08)
  reinstatement_mass ~ gamma(a=2.5, scale=1.2)
  gross_fine_mass = (depositor_count * mass_per_depositor) * purity
  converted_mass = (gross_fine_mass * conversion_yield) * (1 - side_fraction)
  total_reinstated_mass = reinstatement_count * reinstatement_mass
  net_deliverable_mass = converted_mass - total_reinstated_mass
  return net_deliverable_mass < 780
  ```

  A clinic treats a schizophrenic patient under a protocol in which a clinician first conducts an interview and may then hang an albumin infusion.

  ```text
  albumin ~ lognorm(s=0.15, scale=40)
  ```

  ## Task: Time to mend a clinic faucet

  A maintenance worker must mend a leaking faucet beside a wheeled cabinet containing tranquilizer supplies. The faucet’s leak rate is uniformly distributed from 2 to 6 litres per minute. Given the sampled leak rate \(r\), the mean mend duration is \(10 + 2r\) minutes. Conditional on \(r\), the mend duration follows a gamma distribution with shape 4 and scale equal to the conditional mean divided by 4.

  Before starting, the worker spends exactly 2 minutes placing a chock under the cabinet and positioning a flashlight to chin while working. Independently of the leak rate and mend duration, there is a 0.1 probability that the chock slips. This is the only risk event; if it occurs, securing the cabinet again adds exactly 8 minutes.

  ```text
  leak_rate ~ uniform(loc=2, scale=4)

  mend_duration ~ gamma(a=4, scale=mend_scale)

  resecure_duration = chock_slips * 8
  ```

  ## Task: Gray gossip-page printing risk

  A small publisher prints a special gossip page using a dense gray layout. Before each production run, staff jar a fresh batch of gray ink. The total amount of ink available is distributed as `gamma(a=16, scale=0.25)` liters.

  The paper is moistened before printing. Its moisture fraction is distributed as `beta(a=3, b=7)`. Moistening changes the usable proportion of the jarred ink to

  `clip(1 - (0.4 * moisture), 0.7, 1)`.

  Each page requires 0.018 liters of usable ink. Thus, the ink-limited printing capacity is the usable ink divided by 0.018 and rounded down to a whole number of pages.

  The number of gossip pages requested is distributed as `poisson(mu=180)`. The number completed is the minimum of the requested quantity and the ink-limited capacity. Assume the ink quantity, moisture fraction, and requested quantity are mutually independent.

  ```text
  gray_ink ~ gamma(a=16, scale=0.25)
  moisture ~ beta(a=3, b=7)
  orders ~ poisson(mu=180)
  absorption_factor = clip(1 - (0.4 * moisture), 0.7, 1)
  usable_ink = gray_ink * absorption_factor
  print_capacity = floor(usable_ink / 0.018)
  completed = minimum(orders, print_capacity)
  ```
